self_assessment: Added the public User.getUidsByUserslugs(userslugs), which reads the userslug:uid sorted set via db.sortedSetScores and so returns one score (or null) per input slug in order. User.existsBySlug now branches on Array.isArray: for an array it maps those scores to booleans, for a single slug it keeps the existing getUidByUserslug path. Meta.userOrGroupExists detects array input up front, rejects with [[error:invalid-data]] when the single value is falsy or when any array element is falsy (covering '' and undefined), slugifies either the value or every element so human-readable names with spaces or mixed case resolve to stored identifiers, then queries user.existsBySlug and groups.existsBySlug - the latter already handled arrays - and returns a per-index OR for arrays or a plain boolean for a single slug. Verified by extracting the three modified function bodies straight out of the sources and running them against a fake db seeded with one user and two groups: every example from the issue reproduces (single group true, 'John Smith' true, unknown slug false, [false,false], [false,true], [true,true], and ['', undefined] rejecting), plus order preservation with positional duplicate mapping, a one-falsy-element array rejecting, falsy single inputs rejecting, and getUidsByUserslugs returning [7, null] in input order. NodeBB's own suite needs a live redis/mongo plus a built asset bundle so it could not be run; node --check passes on both changed files.
